summary: Planning only. Produced the canonical planning document for Gate-7 Runtime Enforcement and Gate-8 Shell Gate (process containment) consumption integration, re-derived from RDGO-001 v3.0 (section 8 Gate 7, section 9 Gate 8, section 1 table, section 10 durable items, section 13 static-vs-live preflight, section 14, section 15 TOCTOU, section 19 invariants), PBRD-001 v2.0 (section 14 Runtime Enforcement projection, section 4 fourteen facts, section 9 precedence, section 10 gate independence, section 11 process/fs/network/credential distinctions, section 12 POL-005 evolution boundary), RPAC-001 v1.0, RIHAC-001 v2.0, RIASC-001 v3.0, HPAC-001 v2.0, PBPA-001, POL-005 (source), and current src/pcae -- not from summary prose. KEY DERIVED FINDING: there is no production Runtime Enforcement decision engine and no production process-containment / adapter-dispatch mechanism in the repository. 'Runtime Enforcement' exists only as design-only constants (runtime_enforcement_safety_authorization.py -- 12 authorization flag names all default False, 5 safety flag names all default True, AUTH_FLAG_TO_NO_GO / SAFETY_FLAG_TO_NO_GO, RE-NOGO-001..011, non-executing helper predicates) plus Phase 89 simulation models for a different (source-mutation) enforcement domain. 'Shell Gate' exists only as the read-only Phase 88P command classifier (shell_gate.py -- 24 command categories, 26 decision values, build_shell_gate; never executes classified command text; the only subprocess.run call is a governed pcae doctor test-run lock check). FROZEN DECISIONS: Gate 7 = the single independent non-consuming 'final whether-to-invoke' decision over the complete bound runtime_dispatch request (re-evaluates authority freshness, PB evidence, target/capability/posture eligibility, and repository/task/prompt/config currentness); owner = a new runtime_dispatch_gate7.py coordinator (run_gate7_runtime_enforcement) that consumes -- does not reimplement -- the RE no-go vocabulary (there is no verified RE decision logic to duplicate); output = an ephemeral, identity-only, non-serializable, registry-provenanced Gate7Result (decision in {ALLOW, DENY}; no HUMAN_REVIEW at Gate 7), carrying decision/no-go-ids/reason-ids/digests/expiry, NOT an execution token. Gate 8 = the process-containment boundary (re-resolve descriptor/executable/repository/policy drift, refuse any caller shell string, construct and attest one exact bounded launch environment -- executable identity+hash+version, argument vector, cwd, environment allowlist, child-process prohibition/limit, resource/time limit, supervision, network denied, no credentials -- and bind the containment evidence to the invocation); owner = a new runtime_dispatch_gate8.py coordinator (run_gate8_process_containment) that consumes -- does not replace or extend -- the mature 88P shell_gate.py classifier for an executable/argv category cross-check; output = a registry-provenanced Gate8Result (containment_established bool + containment_evidence_digest), NOT an execution token; no dispatch, no consumption. Gate-6 -> Gate-7 handoff = the PBRD-001 section 14 four-item Runtime Enforcement projection (phase-prompt Option C): a registry-provenanced Gate6Decision + the re-resolved Gate5Result projection + current target/status/preflight facts, references/digests not wholesale duplication, with Gate 7 evaluating independently. DENY / HUMAN_REVIEW at Gate 7: unreachable / reject -- only the literal string 'ALLOW' (exact equality, on a registry-provenanced Gate6Decision) permits Gate 7 to proceed to its own evaluation; anti-escalation invariant frozen (no Gate-7 code path converts HUMAN_REVIEW or DENY into a positive Gate7Result); POL-005 DENY => no Gate-7 success. Under the current Observed / observe / unavailable posture Gate 7 ALWAYS rejects: the real production Gate-6 call returns DENY (POL-005), so Gate 7 short-circuits; and even given a hypothetical Gate-6 ALLOW, execution_capability=unavailable matches RE-NOGO-002 and the simulation_only / no_execution / evidence_only / non_authorizing / design_only safety flags match RE-NOGO-011 / RE-NOGO-001 / RE-NOGO-010. No legitimate positive production Gate-7 success is possible today; Gate 8 is therefore structurally unreachable on the production path. Gate-7 and Gate-8 mechanics remain fully implementable and testable -- the negative path IS the production path; the positive branch is exercised only through a clearly-labelled test boundary (the .1R.13 precedent) that does not weaken the production coordinator; no production test bypass. Gate 7 and Gate 8 CONSUME NOTHING (no approval / proof / presentation / challenge / nonce state change; no consumption.json; no call to the runtime_invocation_authority_consumption primitives) -- Gate 9 owns atomic proof + approval consumption. Both coordinators are idempotently repeatable; both results are single-attempt, expiring, and cache-invalid across any relevant input or policy change (RDGO-001 section 8, section 15). Gate-7 -> Gate-8 anti-substitution binding frozen (reject Gate7Result A with effect plan B / invocation B / changed target / changed executable hash vs descriptor pin / changed cwd / changed env allowlist / changed transport / changed descriptor-config / any caller shell string). Gate-8 -> Gate-9 handoff contract FROZEN (the central deliverable that unblocks .1R.14): five exact-object-provenanced trusted objects (Gate8Result via is_gate8_result, Gate7Result via is_gate7_result, Gate6Decision via is_gate6_decision, Gate5Result lineage via is_gate5_result), plus RuntimeDispatchIdentity and RuntimeDispatchRequestConstructionInput and a fresh capability snapshot re-read inside the Gate-9 serialization boundary; six handoff invariants (exact-object provenance at every link; single consistent invocation_id/attempt_id across all five objects; containment_evidence_digest recomputed and compared by Gate 9; in-boundary revalidation of registry/credential/descriptor/presentation/proof/approval/PB/RE/containment state; consumption only at Gate 9's atomic dispatch_attempted write; no effect); assembled in-process only, not serialized, not persisted before Gate 9's own atomic write, not a bearer token. Gate-9 unblocking criteria FROZEN (all 8): (1) Gate-7 implementation complete (.1R.13.2), (2) Gate-7 independently verified (.1R.13.3), (3) Gate-8 implementation complete (.1R.13.4), (4) Gate-8 independently verified (.1R.13.5), (5) the section-16 Gate-8 -> Gate-9 handoff contract frozen and unchanged, (6) no unresolved blocking findings from .1R.13.2-.1R.13.5, (7) runtime still non-executing (not_implemented / Observed / observe / unavailable; POL-005 unchanged; no real adapter) unless separately explicitly human-authorized, (8) independent review of the section-16 handoff contract confirmed at .1R.14 startup. .1R.14 also retains its .1R.9 section 16.2 precondition (satisfied by criteria 1-4). Gate 10 boundary untouched: RDGO-001 section 11 first external effect; no production adapter dispatch exists (runtime_adapter.py abstract + mock_runtime_adapter.py simulation-only, no subprocess/spawn/exec/pty); not created, named, or modified; a future Gate-10 module will consume a Gate9Result, never a Gate7Result/Gate8Result. Runtime capability semantics re-derived: Observed = observe-only, runtime not_implemented; Maximum plugin capability: observe = no invoke/dispatch/mutate capability registrable (0 plugins); Execution capability: unavailable = no code path creates an external process; Runtime Enforcement can never return 'eligible' under this state (RE-NOGO-002); the Gate-7 coordinator owns the capability check, not the Permission Broker (PB permission != runtime capability) and not Gate 8. V-2 / V-3 (RDGO-001 section 4/6 sequence-3 creation wording vs the verified HPAC-REQ-054 step-10 behavior) carried NON-BLOCKING: no Gate-7/Gate-8 impact, no amplification, no sequencing ambiguity (both gates are strictly after Gate 5's confirmation and consume only its output object; both will be AST-guarded to import nothing from hpac_lifecycle / hpac_verifier); no STOP; candidates for the recommended contract-clarification phase. V-4 (PBRD-001 section 4 fact 14 literal 7-field human_authority_binding vs the frozen 3-field production RuntimeDispatchHumanAuthorityBinding -- .1R.13-adjudicated a lossless digest-collapse) carried NON-BLOCKING: Gate 7 and Gate 8 consume only the trusted upstream objects (Gate5Result / Gate6Decision), never the 3-field or 7-field binding directly (planned import/reference-absence test); no direct dependence; PBRD-001 not rewritten; no STOP; candidate for the contract-clarification phase. Prefer invariant tests over permanently-stale frozen-diff assertions. .1R.13.1 performs no test maintenance. O1-O4 / F2-F4 / F7 all carried unchanged, none silently closed: O1 (positive-emission path unreachable under the NON-REAL staging -- inherent, not a defect); O2 (canonical-store trust is path+file integrity, not a writer seal -- the new coordinators must not assume store writer provenance; they rely on exact-object registry membership + the protected-root boundary); O3/F4 (test-name accuracy -- new tests must state which stage rejects); O4 (historical tasks/DONE.md omissions -- untouched, recommend a hygiene pass); F2 (HPAC-REQ-054 Step 4 -- already repaired and verified, prerequisite satisfied); F3 (label debt -- deferred); F7 (the identity registries resist caller-supplied-DATA forgery, NOT same-process arbitrary code execution -- THREAT MODEL NOT BROADENED; the new Gate-7/Gate-8 coordinators, their _GATE7_RESULTS / _GATE8_RESULTS registries, and their consumption of Gate5Result / Gate6Decision all run under the same-account autonomous-agent assumption; no UID / username / process-ownership / stdio / Git identity / PCAE session identity / producer identity is trusted; a process-isolation / hardening chapter remains a legitimate, separate, UNSCHEDULED topic and is NOT a prerequisite for Gate-7 / Gate-8 wiring; both new coordinators and both verification phases MUST state F7's boundary verbatim). Packaging decision (frozen): FOUR SEPARATE SLICES, each followed by an independent verification phase -- Gate 7 (independent whether-to-invoke decision) and Gate 8 (process-containment establishment) have distinct trust boundaries and distinct failure surfaces, and the contracts define them as separate gates with separate owners; coupling is not unavoidable (Gate 8 consumes only Gate 7's ephemeral output object).
